title: Revision 16: Worked answer: guiding technological innovation systems towards sustainable transformation

chapters.title: Read the question
paragraphs: How can technological innovation systems be guided to promote sustainable transformation? Use examples.
The job of this part is to take that question apart before you write. Slides 34 and 35 of Class 9 ask you to show how you read the task.

There are three parts. First, the subject is a technological innovation system. Second, the command is be guided to promote, so the answer needs levers and a direction, not a list of benefits. Third, use examples, so the cases must be Norwegian and you must be able to name their sources. Those were the three parts.

Only Question 1 is compulsory. You then choose Question 2 or Question 3. The two answers are weighted equally, and no aids are allowed. Answers can be tested for plagiarism, so learn the moves and use your own words.
A weaker answer would praise a green technology and stop. A stronger answer would name the weak functions and the policy that aims at them.
One way to say it: By this question, I understand a demand for levers, a direction, and sourced Norwegian cases.
Remember: levers and a direction, then cases you can source.

checks.q: What does be guided to promote ask for?
checks.a: Levers and a direction, not only a list of benefits.

checks.q: What does use examples require here?
checks.a: Norwegian cases, with the readings they come from.

chapters.title: Your plan in one minute
chapters.readings: Class 9, slides 39–41; Hekkert et al. 2007, p. 423; Steen et al. 2024, p. 3
paragraphs: The job of this part is to give you a plan you can say aloud. Slide 39 of Class 9 asks the introduction to show how you read the question and how you will answer it.
Here is the thesis. A technological system is guided toward sustainable transformation when actors rate its functions and aim policy at the weak ones, and when the direction is chosen on purpose.

There are five moves. First, say how you read the question, including the demand for levers. Second, define the system and the functions, including the extra one that capture needs. Third, name the levers, above all guidance of the search and a policy aimed at the weak functions. Fourth, say what goes wrong when the rating is misread or the direction is not chosen. Fifth, use Norway's capture projects and maritime batteries, then close on the question. Those were the five moves.
A memory aid of our own: read it, name the functions, the weak ones, then the cases.
This is the minute to learn by heart. The last chapter will ask for it again. Do not memorise a full script. The marks come from the moves.
Remember: five moves, and the thesis is about rating the functions and choosing the direction.

checks.q: What is the thesis in one sentence?
checks.a: A system is guided when actors rate the functions, aim policy at the weak ones, and choose the direction on purpose.
Use Norway's capture projects and maritime batteries, then close on the question.

chapters.title: The introduction
chapters.readings: Class 9, slides 39, 43; Fløysand et al. 2022, p. 17
paragraphs: The job of this part is the introduction. Slide 39 of Class 9 says to present how you understand the question and how you have chosen to answer it. You may also name one main argument. Slide 43 then checks whether the problem statement follows the question you were given.

In plain words, the opening tells the reader the route. More precisely, you say that guidance is a choice of direction plus work on the functions that are weak. You will define the system, name those levers, and test them on two Norwegian technologies.

Sustainable transformation, as the exam-day sheet takes it from Fløysand and colleagues, citing UNEP, is change that cuts emissions and protects biodiversity. You do not need a longer definition in the first lines. You do need the reader to see that the question asks how a system can be steered toward that change.
A weaker answer would open with a list of policy slogans. A stronger answer would state the route and the two cases in a few lines.
One way to say it: To discuss how such a system can be guided, I will rate the functions, then use two Norwegian cases.
Remember: the introduction states the route and the two cases.

checks.q: What does slide 39 of Class 9 ask the introduction to do?
checks.a: Show how you understand the question and how you have chosen to answer it.

chapters.title: The theory you need
chapters.readings: Hekkert et al. 2007, pp. 416, 421–425, 426; Steen et al. 2024, pp. 2, 3; Schlaile et al. 2017, pp. 4, 5
paragraphs: The job of this part is the theory. Slide 40 of Class 9 says to start from the readings, clarify the concepts, and put those readings to use. Revision six explains the functions in full. Here you only need the pieces this question uses.

In plain words, a technological innovation system is the actors and institutions around one technology, and it can cross regions. Hekkert and colleagues, 2007, citing Carlsson and Stankiewicz, describe a network of agents that create, spread and use a technology under shared institutions. Actors and institutions are not enough. The functions that produce technological change have to be studied too. They list seven, from entrepreneurial activity to the creation of legitimacy.

The functions interact, and the reading names motors. It does not give a sequence in which expectations, investment, experiments and legitimacy pull each other along. Leave that sequence out. Guidance of the search is the function that sets expectations and goals, and so steers which technologies get attention.

Steen and colleagues, 2024, add an eighth function, materialization, because capture needs large plant. Their assessment has three steps. Map the actors, networks and institutions. Rate every function as strong, intermediate or weak. Aim policy at the weak ones.
Schlaile and colleagues keep the aim honest. A conventional path need not serve a social vision. They take the term dedicated innovation system from Pyka.
One way to say it: By guiding such a system, I understand rating the functions and aiming policy at the ones that stay weak.
Remember: seven functions, an eighth for plant, and guidance of the search as the direction-setting function.

checks.q: How many functions do Hekkert and colleagues list?
checks.a: Seven, from entrepreneurial activity to the creation of legitimacy.

checks.q: What are the three steps in Steen and colleagues' assessment?
checks.a: Map the actors, rate every function, and aim policy at the weak ones.

chapters.title: Levers that guide it
chapters.readings: Hekkert et al. 2007, pp. 423, 424; Steen et al. 2024, pp. 3, 9; Njøs et al. 2020, pp. 281, 282; Schlaile et al. 2017, pp. 6, 7
paragraphs: The job of this part is the levers. The command asks how the system can be guided, and slide 40 of Class 9 asks you to put the readings to use on that question.

There are three levers, and each one stays inside a reading. First, guidance of the search. Policy and expectations steer which technologies get attention. That is Hekkert and colleagues. Second, the assessment itself. Rate every function, then aim policy at the weak ones. In the Norwegian capture system those weak ones are market formation, resource mobilization and materialization. Third, a dedicated direction. Schlaile and colleagues ask what to transform, who decides, and who answers. A system pointed at sustainability on purpose is the term they take from Pyka.

Do not turn the second lever into a shopping list. Hekkert and colleagues name market formation as a function. They do not list procurement, regulation, incentives or demonstration as its tools. Where procurement does appear, keep the source. Njøs and colleagues report that public procurement created a market for maritime batteries. That is their finding, not a line from the seven functions.

The model answer picks five functions to strengthen: knowledge, guidance, markets, resources and legitimation. Hekkert and colleagues list seven. They do not select that set of five. Aim at the functions the assessment rates as weak, not at a set you chose in advance.
Remember: guidance of the search, policy aimed at the weak functions, and a direction chosen on purpose.

checks.q: Which three functions are weak in the Norwegian capture system?
checks.a: Market formation, resource mobilization and materialization.

checks.q: What must you not attribute to Hekkert and colleagues?
checks.a: A list of procurement, regulation, incentives and demonstration as the tools of market formation.

chapters.title: What can go wrong
chapters.readings: Steen et al. 2024, p. 9; Schlaile et al. 2017, p. 5; Hekkert et al. 2007, p. 426; Njøs et al. 2020, p. 276
paragraphs: The job of this part is the failure side. Slide 43 of Class 9 looks for analysis that can be critical. A guide that ignores the weak functions does not answer the question.

There are four ways this goes wrong, and each one stays inside a reading. First, a misread rating. Table 3 rates knowledge and legitimation as intermediate, not as strengths. If you call them strengths, you will aim policy at the wrong place. The weak functions are still the market, the resources and the plant. Second, a commercial success that is not a sustainable one. Schlaile and colleagues say a conventional path need not serve a social vision. Third, a warning the informant does not support. The model answer says capture can be used to justify keeping fossil activity. An informant says acceptance rose because capture was not sold that way. Prefer the informant. Fourth, a battery story the course does not contain. Adoption conditions, and a sum of minerals, manufacturing and energy use, are outside the readings. Flag them, and do not grade the technology with them.
The motors are a further caution. The reading expects interactions. It does not give one sequence you can recite as the way the functions pull each other along.
Remember: wrong ratings, a path with no social vision, and two battery warnings that sit outside the course.

checks.q: How does Table 3 rate knowledge and legitimation?
What did the informant say about how capture was sold?
checks.a: Acceptance rose because it was not sold as prolonging fossil activity.

chapters.title: The Norway example
paragraphs: The job of this part is the case. Slide 40 of Class 9 asks for examples that you analyse. Use the two technologies to show the levers, not as decorations.

Norway's capture system is the case for weak functions and for one real exception. Sleipner and Snøhvit are part of that history. Longship supports an integrated chain. The reading names two capture sites, ship transport and offshore storage, and one of the sites is a cement plant. Market formation, resource mobilization and materialization stay weak. Longship and Northern Lights are the main exceptions to that weak materialization. They are large projects being built. They are not proof that the whole system is strong.

Maritime batteries are the case for a lever that worked. The technology is embedded in the region's maritime industry. A cluster set the direction, and public procurement created the market. Njøs and colleagues say the path has to be studied as the link between technological traits and territorial conditions. Neither side alone explains it.

Put the two cases to different jobs. Capture shows where policy should aim. Batteries show a direction and a market that were actually built. Do not grade either one with a life-cycle sum the readings do not contain.
Remember: capture for the weak functions and the Longship exception, batteries for a direction and a market.

checks.q: What does Longship add to the capture chain?
checks.a: Two capture sites, one of them a cement plant, ship transport and offshore storage.

checks.q: What has to be studied together, according to Njøs and colleagues?

chapters.title: Discussion and conclusion
chapters.readings: Class 9, slides 41, 43; Steen et al. 2024, pp. 3, 9; Schlaile et al. 2017, pp. 4, 5
paragraphs: The job of this part is the close. Slide 41 of Class 9 says to sum up what you discussed and to answer the question. Slide 43 adds that the conclusion should link back to theory and to the case, and that you should state a limit.

There are three points to land. First, the lever is the assessment. Map the system, rate the functions, and aim policy at market formation, resource mobilization and materialization, which are the weak ones in the capture case. Second, guidance of the search is how a direction gets chosen, and a dedicated system, the term taken from Pyka, is one that points that direction at sustainability on purpose. The battery market is the example of a direction and a procurement lever that the reading does document. Third, guidance fails when intermediate functions are treated as strengths, or when a commercial path is assumed to serve a social vision.

A limit belongs here. Steen and colleagues note that other interviewees might have produced slightly different ratings, and that capture innovation is international, so a wider geographical lens would help. Say that, and you have shown a boundary.
A weaker answer would end by asking for more support in general. A stronger answer would name the weak functions and the direction, then name the limit.
Remember: answer the question with the weak functions and the chosen direction, then name the limit.

checks.q: What limit should you state if you use the Steen ratings?
checks.a: Other interviewees might have rated the functions differently, and capture innovation is international.

chapters.title: Traps and upgrades
chapters.readings: Hekkert et al. 2007, pp. 421–425, 426; Steen et al. 2024, pp. 2, 9; Njøs et al. 2020, p. 276; Class 9, slide 43
paragraphs: The job of this part is to retire the lines that sound like a policy brief and are not what the course says. Slide 43 rewards readings that are understood.
The first trap is to treat Hekkert's seven functions and Steen's eight as the same list. Instead, say that Steen and colleagues add materialization because capture needs large plant.
The second trap is a chosen set of five functions to strengthen. Instead, use the full list, and aim policy at the functions an assessment rates as weak. The paper does not select that set of five.
The third trap is to call knowledge and legitimacy strengths of the capture system. Instead, use Table 3. Both are intermediate. The weak functions are the market, the resources and the plant.

The fourth trap is a tool list for market formation, or a sequence in which expectations, investment, experiments and legitimacy pull each other along. Instead, say the reading names the function and the motors. It does not give those tools or that sequence.
The fifth trap is a battery life-cycle sum, or a list of adoption conditions, offered as the guide. Instead, leave both out. No course reading makes that assessment.
Remember: rate what the table rates, aim at the weak functions, and leave the outside battery claims outside.

checks.q: What should you say instead of the set of five?
checks.a: Hekkert and colleagues list seven. Aim at the functions the assessment rates as weak.

checks.q: Which battery claims are outside the course?
checks.a: A life-cycle sum, and a list of adoption conditions.

chapters.title: Build it yourself
chapters.readings: Class 9, slides 39–41; Hekkert et al. 2007, p. 423; Steen et al. 2024, p. 9; Njøs et al. 2020, p. 281
paragraphs: The job of this part is to make you say the answer without the script. Pause after each question. Then check yourself.
What does be guided to promote ask you to do? Pause the audio and answer in your head.
Here is the answer. It asks for levers and a direction. A list of benefits does not answer it.
Which function sets the direction, and which functions are weak in the capture system? Pause the audio and answer in your head.
Here is the answer. Guidance of the search sets the direction. Market formation, resource mobilization and materialization are weak. Policy aims at those weak ones.
How does Table 3 rate knowledge and legitimation? Pause the audio and answer in your head.
Here is the answer. Intermediate, not as strengths. Calling them strengths would aim the policy at the wrong place.
Name one sourced lever that built a market in Norway. Pause the audio and answer in your head.
Here is the answer. Njøs and colleagues report that a cluster set a direction for maritime batteries and that public procurement created the market. Keep that lever with their reading.
Say your whole plan aloud in under one minute. Pause the audio and answer in your head.

Here is the answer. There are five moves. First, say how you read the question, including the demand for levers. Second, define the system and the functions, including the extra one that capture needs. Third, name the levers, above all guidance of the search and a policy aimed at the weak functions. Fourth, say what goes wrong when the rating is misread or the direction is not chosen. Fifth, use Norway's capture projects and maritime batteries, then close on the question. Those were the five moves.
Remember: the minute-long plan is the part to know by heart.

checks.q: How many moves are in the plan?

checks.a: Use Norway's capture projects and maritime batteries, then close on the question.
